---
title: "Profile generation"
---

The [level controlled models](level-controlled.qmd) get representative profiles of their water bodies in the `profiles_<water board>` stages.
The profiles -- represented by $A(h)$-relations -- largely determine the retention time of water in a basin,
where the distinction between _doorgaand_ and _bergend_ is crucial:
_doorgaand_ represents flowing water bodies, while
_bergend_ represents stagnant water bodies.
This makes them mainly relevant for water quality simulations.

These profiles also form the basis for the coupling with the groundwater modelling, and their hydro-objects, `verwerkt/profielen/network.gpkg`, guide the [layout](layout.qmd) of the model.
The [gravity controlled models](gravity-controlled.qmd) get their profiles in other ways, see [storage basins](storage-basins.qmd).

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![The hydro-objects of Delfland near Delft. Those on the shortest paths between the crossings of a Basin are doorgaand, and the others bergend.](https://s3.deltares.nl/ribasim-nl/doc-image/figures/profiles-map.png){fig-alt="Map of a network of ditches in which the main routes are thick and blue and the side ditches thin and orange, with one Basin area in grey."}

# Profile generation workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  bgt["BGT water surfaces"] --> width
  hydro["hydro-objects,<br>crossings"] --> paths["doorgaand or bergend,<br>by shortest paths"]
  paths --> width["Width from the<br>BGT surface"]
  width --> depth["Depth from hydrotype,<br>or measured"]
  xs["measured cross-sections"] --> depth
  depth --> ah["A(h) of doorgaand<br>and bergend"]
  ah --> model["Basin / profile,<br>storage Basins"]
```

Profiles are generated per water authority, as
(1) data sources are available per water authority, and
(2) data sources are formatted differently per water authority.

Prior to generating the profiles, the data is preprocessed:

0. Preprocessing of data sources, which includes
    generating `LINESTRING Z`-objects of measured cross-sections,
    sorting the hydro-objects and crossings by their geometry, so that the shortest paths, and with them the profiles, do not depend on the order of the rows, see `path_finder.canonical`,
    removing duplicate hydro-objects,
    repairing hydro-objects along HyDAMO-standards,
    reading the current BGT water surfaces of the area from the national `data/Basisgegevens/BGT/bgt_water.parquet`, see `ribasim_nl.bgt_water`.

Subsequently, the following steps are executed on a per-basin basis:

1.  Select relevant hydro-objects and crossings (i.e., within a basin). Hydro-objects count with their whole length in the basins they overlap by more than $1\,\mathrm{mm}$, and not in those they only touch, see `path_finder.overlaps`;
2.  Generate graph (or network) from hydro-objects (using `networkx`);
3.  Determine the shortest path(s) between crossings, which separates the hydro-objects as _doorgaand_ versus _bergend_;
4.  Couple BGT-polygons to hydro-objects (non-intersecting BGT-polygons will be classified as _bergend_ at a later stage);
5.  Estimate representative width per hydro-object based on coupled BGT-polygon's surface area and circumference;
6.  Estimate representative depth per hydro-object based on width and hydrotope (using a look-up table);
7.  Update representative depth of hydro-objects labelled as _doorgaand_ using measured cross-sections, if available;
8.  Define a trapezoidal cross-sectional profile using the representative width and depth (and a slope of $1:3$, default);
9.  Define the $A(h)$-relation for _doorgaand_ and _bergend_ separately using the length of the hydro-objects;
10. Correct the $A(h)$-relation of _bergend_ by including non-intersecting BGT-polygons' surface areas (as preluded to in 5.);
11. Write two basin profile tables with $A(h)$-relations: one for _doorgaand_, and one for _bergend_.

During model implementation, generated profiles whose maximum area is below $100\,\mathrm{m^2}$ are discarded.
Every retained profile area is then clamped to at least $10\,\mathrm{m^2}$.
If only one of the _doorgaand_ or _bergend_ profiles survives for a basin, it is used for the existing basin without adding a separate storing basin.
When neither profile survives, the model receives a two-point fallback profile with an area of $10\%$ of its basin polygon, subject to the $10\,\mathrm{m^2}$ minimum, at both $2\ \mathrm{m}$ below its target level and at its target level.
If no storing basins remain, implementation still updates the existing basins' profiles and leaves the network unchanged.
This prevents dummy and very small generated profiles from reaching the solver.

Some water boards differ from these steps.
Hollandse Delta and Scheldestromen flag a predefined main route, `gen_profiles.flagged_hydro_objects`, instead of searching shortest paths.
Hollands Noorderkwartier has no measured cross-sections, and Rijnland overrides the depths of its water bodies.

# Profile generation code

The source code is in [`src/ribasim_nl/ribasim_nl/profiles`](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/tree/main/src/ribasim_nl/ribasim_nl/profiles).
The `profiles_<water board>` DVC stages run the two scripts, for instance:

```bash
pixi run dvc repro --pull --single-item profiles_delfland
```

1. [`pipeline/prep_cross_sections.py`](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/tree/main/pipeline/prep_cross_sections.py) preprocesses the measured cross-sections into `LINESTRING Z`-objects.
2. `pipeline/<water board>/02_profiles.py` generates the profile tables, and `implement.set_basin_profiles` sets them in the model, and adds the storage Basins with their ManningResistances.

To run them yourself, per water authority, with the cross-sections first:

```bash
pixi run python pipeline/prep_cross_sections.py <water board>
pixi run python pipeline/<water board>/02_profiles.py
```

The results are in `verwerkt/profielen`:

| File | Content |
|:-----|:--------|
| `network.gpkg` | The hydro-objects with their `main-route`, used for the [layout](layout.qmd). |
| `profielen_doorgaand.csv`, `profielen_bergend.csv` | The tables with the $A(h)$-relations. |
| `intermediate/lines_z.gpkg` | The preprocessed cross-sections. |
| `intermediate/int_output.gpkg` | For inspection: `main-route`, `endpoints`, `bgt`, `hydro-objects`, `basin_profiles_doorgaand` and `basin_profiles_bergend`. |
| `intermediate/graph.gpkg` | For inspection: the graph of the network. |

Only `network.gpkg` is an output of DVC, so the others are there after running the stage yourself.
